ask: C++17. spsc.hpp and bench.cpp: lock-free single-producer/single-consumer bounded queue with std::atomic head/tail, acquire/release ordering, cache-line padding, capacity power of two with mask indexing, try_push/try_pop. bench.cpp pushes 10 million uint64 and verifies ordering, printing throughput. write the files.
prose:
Both files are written and ready to build.

```
g++ -std=c++17 -O2 -pthread -o bench bench.cpp
./bench
```

A few things worth knowing about the design:

`spsc.hpp` — `head_` and `tail_` each live on their own 64-byte cache line. The producer owns `head_` and only acquires `tail_` to check fullness; the consumer owns `tail_` and only acquires `head_` to check emptiness. That one-way acquire/release pair is the minimum synchronisation needed — no seq_cst, no fences.

`bench.cpp` — the producer spins with `yield()` on a full queue, which is realistic for a bounded ring under back-pressure. The consumer verifies strict monotonic ordering and sets `ok` to false on the first violation; it keeps draining regardless so the producer never stalls waiting for a pop. Exit code is 0 on success, 1 on ordering failure.

Expected throughput on a modern x86 or M-series machine is roughly 200–600 M ops/s depending on how the OS schedules the two threads and whether they land on the same physical core. If you want a tighter number, pin both threads to separate cores with `pthread_setaffinity_np` (Linux) or the equivalent.
